ebitda_definition_effect.catalog: baseline.ebitda_definition allowed values: before_sbc or after_sbc. after_sbc is rejected by validate_case. The model subtracts SBC from EBITDA; EBITDA must be before stock-based compensation. SEC/yfinance baselines already add SBC back. If an article EBITDA is after SBC, add SBC back and record before_sbc.
ebitda_definition_effect.sbc_path_change: Default forecast_sbc holds the SBC-to-EBITDA ratio. Year-0 SBC is still Yahoo 2.647812. The year-0 ratio falls from 2.647812/25.89751 = 0.10224 in v04 to 2.647812/26.554099 = 0.09971 in v05. Through the explicit EBITDA-growth years (FY26-FY29) SBC dollars match v04, because sbc[t] = sbc[t-1] * (1+g_ebitda) from the same year-0 SBC. From FY30, v05 SBC is slightly lower than v04, because the ratio at the end of the explicit window is lower (same SBC dollars on a higher EBITDA). before_sbc itself did not change the mechanics: Yahoo was already before_sbc. The path change comes from the higher year-0 EBITDA in the default ratio.
